metadata.description: The name of the Log Analytics workspace with Microsoft Sentinel, where the Altiward setup created the AltiwardOCSF_CL table

properties.displayName: Altiward: a local account appeared while someone was admin
properties.description:
A new local account appeared on a Mac while someone held admin rights: "Admin account
created" (SeverityId 4) or "Local account created". Account is the new account; UserName
is who was admin when it appeared, not necessarily who made it.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.account_created"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, UserName, SeverityId,
    Account = tostring(Ocsf.evidences[0].user.name), Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: admin rights SAP Privileges didn't grant
properties.description:
An account on a Mac became an admin without SAP Privileges granting it, and nothing has
explained it yet. Making the account a permanent admin in Altiward, or a Privileges grant,
explains it and closes the finding (the same finding_info.uid with ActivityId 3), so those
don't alert. Removing the rights (Altiward's automatic removal, a revoke from the console,
or by hand) closes the finding too, with status "Rights removed", but still alerts once:
the rights were held, and nothing explained them.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.admin_out_of_band"
| extend Status = tostring(Ocsf.status)
| summarize Created = countif(ActivityId == 1), arg_max(TimeGenerated, ActivityId, Status, UserName, Message)
    by Uid = tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.uid), DeviceSerial
| where Created > 0 and (ActivityId == 1 or Status == "Rights removed")

properties.displayName: Altiward: one user's admin time in a day over the limit
properties.description:
One person held admin rights through SAP Privileges for longer in a day than you allow:
120 minutes by default. Change MaxAdminMinutes at the top of the query to tune it, or set
it to Privileges' AdminBudget to report the same limit from your SIEM. Unlike
AdminBudget, it covers Macs on Privileges 2.6 and earlier, and moving a Mac's clock
forward doesn't reset it.
It runs daily and reports the last complete day in UTC. An elevation lasts until the next
grant or revoke for the same user on the same Mac, or until now if there's none yet. One
that crosses midnight counts towards each day for its part in that day. Time on two Macs
at once counts twice.
Works with the Altiward agent's events and altiward-forwarder's. The forwarder's records
have no session ID and can't show rights kept past their expiry, so its elevations count
up to their expiry at most. Admin rights Privileges didn't grant aren't counted: the
out-of-band rule reports those.
properties.query:
// The limit: minutes of admin rights per user per UTC day. Your AdminBudget, to match it.
let MaxAdminMinutes = 120;
let DayEnd = startofday(now());
let DayStart = DayEnd - 1d;
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 3005 and ActivityId in (1, 2) and toint(Ocsf.status_id) == 1
| extend DeviceUid = tostring(Ocsf.device.uid)
| sort by DeviceUid asc, UserName asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend End = iff(next(DeviceUid) == DeviceUid and next(UserName) == UserName,
    next(TimeGenerated), now())
| where ActivityId == 1
| extend Expires = unixtime_milliseconds_todatetime(tolong(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.expires_time))
| extend End = iff(tostring(Ocsf.metadata.product.name) == "Altiward Forwarder" and isnotnull(Expires),
    min_of(End, Expires), End)
| extend Minutes = (min_of(End, DayEnd) - max_of(TimeGenerated, DayStart)) / 1m
| where Minutes > 0
| summarize AdminMinutes = round(sum(Minutes)), Elevations = count(),
    Macs = make_set(coalesce(DeviceSerial, DeviceUid)) by UserName, Day = DayStart
| where AdminMinutes > MaxAdminMinutes

properties.displayName: Altiward: a Mac stopped checking in
properties.description:
The Altiward server hasn't heard from a Mac for longer than the console's setting allows
(72 hours by default; Basis no_contact, Medium). With Intune connected, it also raises one
early when Intune has heard from the Mac at least 2 hours after its last check-in with
Altiward (Basis mdm_check_in, High): the Mac is on and online, so its agent may have been
removed or stopped. MdmLastCheckIn is Intune's last check-in from the Mac, AdminMembers
the Mac's admins at its last check-in. Message also names any new key for the Mac waiting
for approval, which the agent can't report with until it is approved. The Mac checking in
again closes the finding with the same finding_info.uid, so only Macs still silent at the
end of the hour alert.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.agent_silent"
| extend Basis = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.basis),
    LastSeenAt = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.last_seen_at),
    MdmLastCheckIn = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.mdm_last_check_in),
    AdminMembers = strcat_array(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.admin_members, ", ")
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, ActivityId, Basis, LastSeenAt, MdmLastCheckIn, AdminMembers, Message)
    by Uid = tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.uid), DeviceSerial
| where ActivityId == 1
| extend AlertSeverity = iff(Basis == "mdm_check_in", "High", "Medium")

properties.displayName: Altiward: the console's break-glass token was used
properties.description:
Someone signed in to the Altiward console, or acted in it, with a console token while
single sign-on is on: the break-glass login, meant for when the identity provider is down.
UserName is break-glass: and the token's fingerprint. Only the console's records match.
Records that arrive up to 7 days late still alert, once: the rule searches the last 7
days of records and alerts on those ingested in the last hour.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
| where ClassUid in (6003, 3002) and UserName startswith "break-glass:"
| where tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.event_type) startswith "console."
| extend Action = iff(ClassUid == 3002, tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.action), tostring(Ocsf.api.operation))
| project TimeGenerated, UserName, Action, DeviceSerial, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: a grant or revoke the admin group contradicts
properties.description:
SAP Privileges reported a grant or revoke that the Mac's admin group doesn't show, which
can mean someone is tampering with the report. The detail says what the agent found.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 3005 and toint(Ocsf.status_id) == 1 and SeverityId >= 3
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, UserName, Message, Detail = tostring(Ocsf.status_detail)

properties.displayName: Altiward: a device key was replaced without approval
properties.description:
A new key replaced a Mac's active key without approval. This only happens when
re-enrolment approval is off. Check whether the owner expected the reinstall or key
change and compare independent inventory. If unexpected, revoke the new key, enable
approval and rotate the enrolment token. Hardware UUIDs are client claims.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 6003 and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.event_type) == "agent.enrollment"
    and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.state) == "replaced"
| extend Token = tostring(Ocsf.actor.user.name), DeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.device_id),
    PreviousDeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.previous_device_id),
    HardwareUuidMatches = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.hardware_uuid_matches),
    KeyStorage = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.key_storage)
| project TimeGenerated, TenantUid, DeviceSerial, Token, DeviceId, PreviousDeviceId, HardwareUuidMatches, KeyStorage, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: a device key is waiting for approval
properties.description:
A new key is waiting for approval. This can be normal after a reinstall, and for every
new Mac when Approve every new Mac is on in Altiward. Before approving,
check the Mac's last check-in in Altiward, HardwareUuidMatches and whether its owner
expects the change. An empty HardwareUuidMatches means there was no active key to
compare, as for a new Mac. Hardware UUIDs are client claims, not proof of the Mac's
identity. With Intune connected, MdmCheck is what Intune said about the device ID the Mac
sent: mismatch (High) means Intune has that ID under another serial or on another
platform, so it is another Mac's or another device's, and the key waits for approval
whatever the settings. Other keys are Medium.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 6003 and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.event_type) == "agent.enrollment"
    and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.state) == "pending"
| extend Token = tostring(Ocsf.actor.user.name), DeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.device_id),
    PreviousDeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.previous_device_id),
    HardwareUuidMatches = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.hardware_uuid_matches),
    KeyStorage = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.key_storage),
    MdmCheck = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.mdm_check)
| extend AlertSeverity = iff(MdmCheck == "mismatch", "High", "Medium")
| project TimeGenerated, TenantUid, DeviceSerial, Token, DeviceId, PreviousDeviceId, HardwareUuidMatches, KeyStorage,
    MdmCheck, AlertSeverity, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: more than 10 elevations by one user in 7 days
properties.description:
One person asked SAP Privileges for admin rights more than 10 times in 7 days. Either
they need a different way to do their work, or the rights are being used for something
else. Works with the Altiward agent's events and altiward-forwarder's.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 3005 and ActivityId == 1 and toint(Ocsf.status_id) == 1
| summarize Elevations = count() by UserName
| where Elevations > 10

properties.displayName: Altiward: a SAP Privileges grant claim was refused or not confirmed
properties.description:
The Altiward agent refused a claim from SAP Privileges' hook, or accepted one that
Privileges' own log doesn't back. Someone who already holds admin rights can run the hook
by hand to make those rights look granted, or to keep a Privileges session going, so this
is an attack signal, not a misconfiguration. Kind says what was claimed (grant, renewal or
give_back), Outcome whether it was refused or accepted_unconfirmed, and Reason why.
CallerUid is the UID of the process that sent the claim.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.tamper.grant_claim"
| extend Account = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.user), Kind = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.kind),
    Outcome = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.outcome), Reason = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.reason),
    CallerUid = toint(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.caller_uid)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, Account, Kind, Outcome, Reason, CallerUid, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: persistence appeared while someone was admin
properties.description:
A launch daemon or agent, an SSH key, a sudoers rule or another way back in appeared on a
Mac while someone held admin rights. Each file is a row, to look up in your EDR's data for
the same Mac; Session ties it to the elevation.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.persistence_detected"
| mv-expand Evidence = Ocsf.evidences
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, UserName, Session = tostring(Ocsf.metadata.correlation_uid),
    Path = tostring(Evidence.file.path), Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: a Mac account's Platform SSO link may now name someone else
properties.description:
A Mac account's Platform SSO link changed in a way that may put the account on someone
else's UPN: it moved to another account, or it was added when the account was last linked
to someone else, when another Mac account has the same link, or while someone held admin
rights. Altiward takes each person's UPN from these links, so later elevations on that
account carry the new UPN. Account is the Mac account, PreviousUpn the account it was linked
to before (empty for none) and Upn the one it is linked to now. Check with the account's
owner, and in your identity provider, that the new link is theirs. Other links added or
removed (altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link), as registering for Platform SSO does, don't
alert.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link_changed"
| extend Account = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.user),
    PreviousUpn = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.previous_upn), Upn = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.upn)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, Account, PreviousUpn, Upn, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: admin rights outlived their expiry
properties.description:
Admin rights were still held after SAP Privileges' expiry, usually because its timer was
stopped. Altiward raises it whether or not it removed them: SeverityId 4 means it
couldn't.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) == "altiward.rights_after_expiry"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceSerial, UserName, SeverityId, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: a rotated device key was used
properties.description:
A device key that the Mac had already replaced by rotation was used again. Two copies
of one Mac's device key exist: the Mac's, and a copy made from a backup, a disk image
or a migration. When RevokedDeviceId is set, Altiward has revoked the lineage's key,
so neither holder has a working key, and the Mac enrols again by itself. When it is
empty, nothing was revoked: the key was replaced more than 30 days ago, or this key
already caused a revocation. A copy carries the Mac's serial number and hardware UUID,
so they don't tell its key from the Mac's. Run altiward-agent status on the Mac
through your MDM, approve only the pending key whose fingerprint in Enrollments
matches the key fingerprint it prints, and reject the others. When RevokedDeviceId is
empty and the pending key is the Mac's, the active key, if there is one, isn't the
Mac's: revoke it, then approve the Mac's key. Look for where the copy came from:
backups, disk images and Migration Assistant. A Mac restored from a backup older than
its last rotation also raises this alert, and its fresh key is genuine.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 6003 and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.event_type) == "agent.enrollment"
    and tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.state) == "rotated_key_used"
| extend DeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.device_id),
    KeyFingerprint = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.key_fingerprint),
    RotatedTo = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.rotated_to),
    RevokedDeviceId = tostring(Ocsf.unmapped.altiward.detail.revoked_device_id)
| project TimeGenerated, TenantUid, DeviceSerial, DeviceId, KeyFingerprint, RotatedTo, RevokedDeviceId, Message

properties.displayName: Altiward: a tamper check is failing
properties.description:
One of the Altiward agent's integrity checks failed on a Mac, such as SAP Privileges'
settings no longer being managed. A failure and its fix share finding_info.uid, so only
checks still failing at the end of the hour alert. A refused or unconfirmed grant claim
(altiward.tamper.grant_claim) and a Platform SSO link that may now name someone else
(altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link_changed) are left out: their own rules alert on them
sooner, at High. So are other Platform SSO links added or removed
(altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link), which mostly record people registering for Platform
SSO.
properties.query:
AltiwardOCSF_CL
| where ClassUid == 2004 and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) startswith "altiward.tamper."
    and tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.analytic.name) !in ("altiward.tamper.grant_claim",
    "altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link", "altiward.tamper.platform_sso_link_changed")
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, ActivityId, SeverityId, Message) by Uid = tostring(Ocsf.finding_info.uid), DeviceSerial
| where ActivityId == 1
